note: Hand-authored, not `cfusa tara`-generated -- cfusa tara only emits a placeholder skeleton with no input-file mechanism to seed real content (see ROADMAP.md milestone 57 and CYBERSECURITY.md section 3). This TARA fully replaces the pre-TC18 threat model (command/status channel, zone registry, OTA firmware transfer -- firmware.h/firmware.c were DEPRECATE-removed at milestone 83 and have no TC18 counterpart) as of ROADMAP.md milestone 85 (Phase 22 re-certification pass), re-derived against the actual TC18 attack surface: request/response streams, the discovery/lifecycle bootstrap sequence, and MACsec's role now that tls.c is deprecated. Update by hand when threats, mitigations, or their implementation status change -- do not run `cfusa tara` over this file.

assets.description: TC18 request/response traffic on a request stream (register-map writes, per-endpoint-type requests) addressed by (stream_id, byte_bus_id)
Response/ack queue and status/telemetry data returned to the caller over a stream's response queue
Discovery/lifecycle bootstrap sequence -- EP0 root-client grant, discovery claim, and the HW/RCP configuration manifest applied while HW_UNCONFIGURED
Link-layer transport carrying AVTPDUs (native Ethernet, IEEE1722-over-UDP/IP, or CAN(FD/XL)-as-network)

threats.threat: An attacker with transport access injects forged ACF requests impersonating a legitimate caller identity (request injection / spoofing).
threats.cybersecurity_goal: No request shall be forwarded to an endpoint unless the caller's asserted identity is permitted for that endpoint/request-type by the loaded policy.
threats.notes: rcp_authz_policy_permit() (REAL, working, exercised by test_authz.c) rejects any identity/address/request-type combination not in the policy table. Its identity input is still a caller-supplied short string label (certificate CN or pre-shared key label per authz.h's own file header); full certificate-chain validation remains the responsibility of whichever link-layer security control (MACsec) is in effect. This library's own default posture (mock/sim/udp/shmem transports) supplies no cryptographic identity source of its own -- see TS-004.

threats.threat: An attacker captures a previously-valid request and replays it to cause unintended repeated actuation or a stale response.
threats.cybersecurity_goal: No request carrying a previously-seen sequence number shall be accepted.
threats.requirement_ref: REQ-E2E-028, REQ-E2E-029 -- see H-004/SG-004 in HARA.md
threats.notes: MITIGATED (OPT-IN), updated 2026-08-20 (issue #606/#601). TC18 Sec12.7.7 Table 24 itself defines rx_enforce_seq/rx_seq_safestate_enable (0x000D bits 1/2); rcp_e2e_seq_evaluate()/rcp_e2e_seq_tracker_t (e2e.c/e2e.h) implement it and are wired into mock.c's reference dispatch composition (frame_seq_gate_admits(), evaluated once per AVTPDU frame, before any ACF member is processed) -- REQ-E2E-028/REQ-E2E-029 are both status: implemented, scope: tc18 (a real spec mechanism, not a c-RCP-specific extension). This is opt-in, not automatic: an integrator must enable the config bits via regmap.h and must replicate mock.c's admit()+evaluate() composition in their own real, I/O-attached dispatch loop -- this library ships no networked dispatcher of its own. Residual risk even when enabled: tracker state is per-process/per-restart (no persistence -- a replay immediately after a restart is not detected), RFC 1982 forward-window comparison only distinguishes a sequence gap in [1,127] from ordinary 8-bit wraparound, and detection granularity is per-AVTPDU-frame, not per-ACF-message. See include/rcp/e2e.h's own file header for the full scope statement. Superseded prior note: this entry previously read 'OPEN, UNMITIGATED' -- that was accurate through issue #338 (v0.322.0) but is stale now; retained here in spirit only via this note's own history, not as a live claim.

threats.threat: An attacker claims the EP0 root-client grant during discovery/bootstrap, or writes HW/RCP configuration it does not legitimately own, hijacking the server's configuration before a legitimate caller establishes its claim.
threats.cybersecurity_goal: Only a caller holding a valid, unexpired discovery claim (or, post-bootstrap, an authorized EP0 root-client/owning-stream writer context) shall be permitted to write HW/RCP configuration.
threats.requirement_ref: REQ-DISC-017, REQ-DISC-018, REQ-DISC-019, REQ-DISC-021, REQ-RMAP-009, REQ-RMAP-010, REQ-RMAP-011, REQ-RMAP-012
threats.notes: rcp_discovery_claim_note_request() grants an open (unheld or lapsed) claim to the first requester and does not preempt an already-active claimant (REAL, working, exercised by test_discovery.c); rcp_discovery_claim_note_config_write() rejects a config write from a non-claimant without mutating state. This is a first-claimant-wins model with a configurable timeout, not an identity-verified one -- it prevents a second attacker from displacing an already-bonded legitimate claimant, but does not itself cryptographically authenticate the first claimant to arrive during a server's HW_UNCONFIGURED bootstrap window. Closing that residual gap requires the same link-layer authentication (MACsec) TS-004 already tracks as absent from this library's own posture.

threats.threat: An attacker with link-layer access eavesdrops on or tampers with AVTPDU traffic in the absence of MACsec, since this library implements no link-layer authentication or encryption of its own.
threats.attack_vector: physical (link-layer access to the native Ethernet/AVB segment or the IEEE1722-over-UDP/IP path)
threats.cybersecurity_goal: Link-layer authentication (MACsec, 802.1AE) shall be enforced by the deployment on any transport carrying safety-relevant requests.
threats.requirement_ref: None -- deployment-level control; see CYBERSECURITY.md Layer 1
threats.notes: OPEN, by design out of this library's own scope: the TC18 spec's own security control is MACsec, an explicitly product-specific/opaque link-layer configuration block (ROADMAP.md's tls.h/tls.c DEPRECATE disposition), not something a portable C99 protocol library implements itself. This library's own transports (udp.c, avtp.c, shmem.c) carry AVTPDUs with no authentication or encryption layer of their own; every prior TLS-based mitigation this project's pre-TC18 TARA cited (tls.c) is gone, and no replacement is implemented here -- integrators are expected to supply MACsec at the link layer, matching the same secure-by-refusal (not secure-by-a-fallback) posture the retired tls.c stub already established.

threats.threat: An attacker floods an endpoint with non-safety-tagged requests to exhaust its finite request-queue capacity and starve legitimate traffic.
threats.cybersecurity_goal: A flood of non-safety-tagged requests shall not exhaust an endpoint's processing capacity; safety-tagged requests shall remain exempt by default.
threats.notes: rcp_ratelimit_limiter_allow()'s per-(stream_id, byte_bus_id) token bucket (REAL, working, exercised by test_ratelimit.c) exempts safety-tagged (MSB-set) requests by default, re-anchored on e2e.h's rcp_e2e_is_safety_request() now that the retired RCP_PRIORITY_CRITICAL client-assigned tag has no TC18 counterpart. The only threat in this TARA with a complete, working, library-level mitigation with no external backend dependency.
